items.title: Ghana launches Social Protection Act regulations and Affirmative Action Gender Equity Regulations
items.description: Ghana has taken a significant step towards strengthening social protection and advancing gender equity with the launch of three key legal instruments by the Vice President, H.E. Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, in Accra on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. The instruments are the Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148), the Social Protection Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2521), and the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2522). Organised by the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP), the launch was held under the theme, “Building an Inclusive, Equitable and Resilient Ghana: From Legislation to Results.” Delivering the keynote address, the Vice President said the success of the new frameworks would be measured by their impact on the lives of Ghanaians. She noted that the Social Protection Act provides a legal foundation for a coordinated national system covering social assistance, social insurance, emergency support, the Social Protection Fund, and mechanisms for complaints and redress. She added that the accompanying Regulations would guide implementation, while the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Regulations would help institutions meet their obligations to advance women’s participation in leadership and decision-making. The Vice President called for effective implementation, accountability and the efficient use of public resources to ensure that people experiencing poverty and vulnerability receive appropriate support and that women have fair opportunities to contribute to national development. The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Hon. Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, described the launch as both an achievement and a responsibility for the Ministry. She acknowledged the years of advocacy and consultation involving women’s groups, persons with disabilities, older persons and other stakeholders in shaping the instruments. The Minister outlined five commitments to guide implementation: making the laws accessible in plain language and local languages; providing institutions with practical guidelines, reporting templates and training; strengthening data, targeting and coordination systems; improving complaints and feedback mechanisms; and publishing regular progress reports. She also pledged that the Ministry and its agencies would fully comply with the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Regulations. She urged social welfare officers, community development officers, gender desk officers and other frontline personnel to perform their duties with fairness, professionalism and compassion, noting that their work would be critical to translating the laws into meaningful results for citizens. The importance of social protection was illustrated through the story of an older widow whose husband’s death left her struggling to provide for her children and keep them in school. Without a salary or pension and with limited mobility due to age, she relied on support to meet her household’s basic needs. Her experience highlighted the role of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme in supporting vulnerable households and the need to link social assistance with livelihood opportunities to build lasting resilience. Representatives of UNICEF and the World Bank commended Ghana for this milestone and reaffirmed their support for strengthening social protection and gender equity. They emphasised the importance of reliable data, effective programme delivery, and connecting social assistance to services, skills development, livelihoods and financial inclusion. The launch brought together representatives of Parliament, traditional authorities, public institutions, development partners, civil society, organised labour, the private sector, women’s groups, persons with disabilities, youth organisations, academia and the media. The Vice President subsequently unveiled the three instruments, marking the beginning of a renewed focus on implementation. The priority now is to ensure that the new legal frameworks translate into tangible improvements in the lives of Ghanaians.

items.title: Taraba varsity ASUU begins indefinite strike over arrears
items.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — Academic activities at Taraba State University (TSU), Jalingo, have been disrupted following the declaration of an indefinite strike by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) over the state government’s alleged failure to implement the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU remuneration framework. The strike, which took effect on Monday, October 12, 2026, followed the expiration of a two-week grace period granted to the administration of Governor Agbu Kefas to meet the union’s demands. The ASUU-TSU Branch Chairman, Dr Joshua Garba Mbave, announced the industrial action in a statement issued in Jalingo, saying the union’s congress decided to down tools after exhausting avenues for dialogue, appeals and extensions. Mbave said the strike was driven by two major demands: immediate implementation of the 2025 FGN-ASUU remuneration agreement at the university and payment of all outstanding salary arrears from January 2026. He said the union had exercised restraint since February 2026 while engaging the state government on the matter. According to him, the engagement led to the constitution of a verification committee to assess the existing salary structure and the level of implementation across universities in the North-East. The union chairman said the committee’s findings indicated that other universities in the region had achieved full implementation of the salary scale. He added that the tripartite committee submitted its report, detailing the financial implications of the implementation, on September 24. Mbave further said the state government failed to fulfil its commitment despite an appeal from the Office of the Head of Service seeking an additional 14 days to address the matter. “The Union wishes to state that it has demonstrated considerable patience, responsibility and commitment to dialogue throughout this process,” the statement said. It added that the continued delay in implementing the agreement, despite the completion of the verification process, had compelled the union to commence the strike. ASUU-TSU, however, said the industrial action did not amount to a rejection of dialogue, expressing its readiness to engage the state government and other relevant stakeholders. “Such engagement, however, must be sincere, timely and directed towards achieving a definite resolution,” the union said. It urged the Taraba State Government to respect the processes already concluded and take immediate steps to implement the remuneration framework and settle outstanding salary arrears. The union also appealed to the public to understand its position, describing the dispute as a struggle for fairness, the dignity of university workers and respect for agreements reached in good faith. items.title: Coastal highway: Atiku challenges Tinubu over alleged $20bn loan plan
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain changes to the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, demanding a full account of contract payments and clarification of an alleged plan to borrow up to $20 billion for payments reportedly connected to the project. Atiku said the reported rerouting of sections of the highway had raised questions about the original contract, the cost of the revised design and whether Nigerians were being asked to shoulder additional debt without knowing what had already been paid or what remained to be done. He also alleged that lawmakers were being pressured to approve the anticipated loan request. In a statement on Monday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of changing the project’s direction without providing Nigerians with a full account of the financial implications. “Tinubu sold Nigerians a coastal highway. Now his Minister says parts of it will follow an existing road inland. That is not a minor adjustment to a drawing. It strikes at the promise used to sell this enormous project. When the route changes, the price must be opened. When the work changes, the payments must be explained,” he said. Atiku called on Works Minister David Umahi to publish the original engineering studies and revised designs, questioning whether the government had adequately assessed the terrain, bridges and flood risks before awarding the contract. He also demanded a breakdown of work removed from the original contract, payments already made and the revised project cost. “You cannot change the work and refuse to change the bill,” Atiku said. The former vice president further challenged Tinubu to clarify whether his administration was preparing to seek a loan of up to $20 billion from the National Assembly and whether any portion of the proposed borrowing would finance payments connected to Hitech Construction Company. “Do not hide a contractor’s bill inside a national borrowing request. Publish the proposed loan, the contract it would finance and the record of what has already been paid. If no such request exists, say so plainly and on the record,” he said. Atiku also alleged that some lawmakers had been warned that funds for their election campaigns would be withheld unless they approved the anticipated loan request. He urged the National Assembly leadership to investigate the allegation and ensure lawmakers had access to the proposed loan terms and project accounts before voting. “We are informed that some lawmakers have been warned that funds for their election campaigns will be withheld unless they pass this request with the speed of light. Who is making that threat? Whose money is being promised or withheld? And why should any legislator’s campaign depend on voting to put Nigerians in debt?” he asked. He called for the publication of the original feasibility and environmental studies, route maps, Bills of Quantities, contract variations, Bureau of Public Procurement approvals, payment certificates and all borrowing proposals tied to the highway. He also demanded a public hearing before the National Assembly considers further financing. Atiku linked the controversy to what he described as a pattern of policy inconsistency under Tinubu, arguing that Nigerians already struggling with the cost-of-living crisis should not be saddled with additional financial obligations arising from poorly explained project changes. “This is the policy inconsistency that has defined Tinubu’s government and made an already severe cost of living crisis harder for Nigerians to bear. Announce a plan. Change it without a full accounting. Then present the public with a bigger bill,” he said. The allegations, if substantiated, could intensify scrutiny of the federal government’s management of the coastal highway, particularly over contract variations, public borrowing and the role of the National Assembly in authorising further financial commitments. Atiku insisted that no additional borrowing should proceed without full disclosure of the project’s contractual obligations, payments made and the justification for the proposed financing. The post Coastal highway: Atiku challenges Tinubu over alleged $20bn loan plan appeared first on Vanguard News .

Tinubu asked me to claim Adelabu as my ministerial choice, I refused — Makinde
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has said President Bola Tinubu asked him to take ownership of Adebayo Adelabu’s ministerial appointment after rejecting his recommendation of former Oyo state commissioner for finance, Bimbo Adekanmbi. Makinde made this disclosure on Sunday during a media chat with Fresh FM in Ibadan, where he also discussed the G5 governors’ alliance with Tinubu ahead of the 2023 presidential election. The governor said Tinubu had initially asked him to recommend a development economist for the budget and economic planning portfolio. He said he nominated Adekanmbi because he believed the former commissioner had played a significant role in stabilising the administration of former Oyo State governor Abiola Ajimobi. Makinde said Tinubu later informed him that he had decided to appoint Adelabu, whom he contested against in the 2019 Oyo governorship election. Recounting the conversation, Makinde said, “I said, ‘Okay, I know Bayo.’ I contested against Bayo in 2019. He is a first-class material.’ “And then the president eventually said, ‘Well, since I’ve taken this decision to appoint Bayo, you should go and take ownership of him, like go out and say it was your choice.’” The governor said he rejected the suggestion, insisting that the appointment should be acknowledged as Tinubu’s decision. “So I said, ‘No, sir. Bayo is your choice, and let it be known to the people that it is your choice. “‘I’m supposed to help you by nominating people who can add value to your administration. If you’ve seen somebody who can do that, that’s good.’” Makinde said he later discovered that other governors had also been asked to adopt ministerial nominees selected by Tinubu. “The point I’m trying to make is that most of my colleagues, not just those in the G5, my governor colleagues, right, were given people and asked to adopt those people as theirs,” he said. Makinde also said most members of the G5, a group of five governors elected on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), did not receive ministerial appointments under Tinubu’s administration. “The G5, minus, of course, Wike, was not given ministerial appointments,” he said. The G5 comprised Makinde, Nyesom Wike, Samuel Ortom, Ifeanyi Ugwuanyi and Okezie Ikpeazu. The governors opposed the PDP’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, ahead of the 2023 election amid disagreements over the party’s leadership. Makinde, whose second and final term ends in May 2027, is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). At the APM Northeast 2027 Town Hall Meeting in Yola, Adamawa State, on Sunday, he promised to establish a four-year transitional Government of National Unity (GNU) if elected president in 2027. items.title: Mahama swears in Emelia Afi Agbenyo, Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as EC Deputy Commissioners
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has sworn in Emelia Afi Agbenyo and Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission (EC). Their appointments fill vacancies in the Commission’s leadership following the departure of two former deputy chairpersons. During the event at the Jubilee House on Monday, President Mahama urged them to exercise “fairness, restraint, and fidelity to the law.” “As president, I expect no preferential treatment from the electoral commission for myself, my party, or my government. I expect an institution that applies the same standards to everyone and protects Ghanaians’ right to choose their leaders freely,” he added. Dr Bossman Eric Asare, who was responsible for Corporate Affairs, resigned effective July 31, 2026, to return to academia at the University of Ghana. Samuel Tettey, who oversaw Operations, also exited the Commission after reaching the mandatory retirement age. Read Also: Former EC Finance Director and KNUST Law Lecturer Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah appointed Deputy Chair Dr Asamoah is a lawyer, chartered accountant and lecturer at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). He has more than 17 years of experience spanning electoral administration, public service, legal practice and academia. Before his appointment, he held several positions at the EC, including Director of Finance, Director of the Training Centre and Head of Audit. He also participated in the administration of several electoral exercises, including the 2012 and 2016 general elections. The appointments come as the Commission continues its work in managing Ghana’s electoral processes and preparations for future elections.

items.title: Wetland communities in Northern Ghana face a hotter, flood-prone future as climate risks intensif
items.description: From scorching heat and prolonged drought to devastating floods and unpredictable rainfall, Ghana’s vulnerable wetland communities face an increasingly uncertain future. New research, however, suggests that restoring nature and empowering local communities could help turn the tide against climate change. Ghana’s wetland communities could face mounting threats to their livelihoods, food security and economic stability as rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, heavier storms and flash flooding intensify, according to findings from an international climate research initiative. The findings emerge from the Addressing Climate Vulnerability through Nature-Based Solutions using Transdisciplinary Engagement of Wetland Communities (AV-STEC) project, which brings together the Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Research at the University of Ghana, Naturama in Burkina Faso, York University in Canada, and the Stockholm Environment Institute in the United States. The AVSTEC team leaders include Emerita Professor Yaa Ntiamoa-Baidu (CBCR); Prof Christopher Gordon (University of Ghana); Prof Joseph Mensah, York University; Mr. Idrissah Zeba, Naturama, Burkina Faso; and Dr. Mary Thompson, START, USA. The project aims to strengthen climate resilience by connecting scientific research with local knowledge and helping communities develop practical, inclusive and sustainable adaptation strategies. A CLIMATE WARNING THAT CANNOT BE IGNORED Climate projections examined by the project point to a future of increasing extreme heat, greater rainfall variability, heavier storm bursts and flash flooding. Communities dependent on agriculture and natural resources could face multiple climate threats, sometimes within the same season. Farmers may struggle with prolonged dry conditions, only to see intense rainfall flood their fields and destroy crops. Such overlapping hazards can deepen poverty, threaten food production and place additional pressure on households already struggling to cope with environmental changes. The findings reinforce the need for climate planning that looks beyond individual disasters to address the interconnected risks affecting people, water systems and agricultural livelihoods. WHY EMERGENCY RELIEF IS NOT ENOUGH While emergency assistance can provide essential support after floods, the research highlights the limitations of relying primarily on relief after disasters have occurred. Instead, it points to Nature-Based Solutions, including catchment reforestation, green belts and wetland restoration, as important approaches to strengthening long-term resilience. Healthy wetlands and restored landscapes can help retain and manage water, support biodiversity and reduce some of the impacts associated with flooding. These measures, alongside effective planning and early-warning systems, could help communities prepare for climate hazards rather than continually recover from them. The research therefore calls for a shift towards addressing the underlying causes of vulnerability, not simply managing the consequences. SOLAR-POWERED IRRIGATION OFFERS FARMERS AN ALTERNATIVE Agriculture is another major concern. When farming depends heavily on rainfall, unpredictable weather can undermine production and household incomes. The AV-STEC project is working with communities to co-design dry-season, solar-powered irrigated agro-ecological systems. These initiatives seek to reduce dependence on rainfall and create opportunities for agricultural production during drier periods. The emphasis on co-design is significant: communities are involved in developing solutions intended to respond to their actual needs, circumstances and knowledge. WOMEN MUST HAVE A VOICE IN CLIMATE SOLUTIONS The findings also highlight the importance of gender-responsive climate policies. Men and women can experience climate-related hardship differently, depending on their economic opportunities, household responsibilities and access to resources. The project emphasizes women’s financial independence and the need to expand access to credit facilities, business training and economic opportunities. Without deliberate efforts to address these differences, climate adaptation programmes risk leaving vulnerable groups behind and potentially worsening existing inequalities. 89% OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS ARE WILLING TO PARTICIPATE One encouraging finding is that 89 per cent of local community members expressed willingness to participate in flood-mitigation and nature-based adaptation initiatives . The figure suggests considerable potential for community-led action, provided residents receive meaningful opportunities, resources and institutional support to participate. The project identifies collaboration among research partners, government involvement, local ownership and effective consultation as important enabling factors. However, challenges remain, including limited budgets, shortened project timelines, geographical constraints and the influence of the Bagre Dam’s operation on downstream water conditions. GHANA AND BURKINA FASO MUST WORK TOGETHER Because the water systems cross national boundaries, climate resilience also requires cooperation between Ghana and Burkina Faso. The project is supporting renewed dialogue on transboundary water management and early-warning cooperation following the collapse of the joint bilateral technical committee in 2011. Stronger coordination could help communities and institutions better understand shared water-related risks and improve preparedness as rainfall patterns become increasingly unpredictable. FROM RESEARCH TO ACTION The AV-STEC findings offer both a warning and an opportunity. Climate risks are placing pressure on livelihoods, but communities have demonstrated a willingness to participate in practical responses. The next challenge is translating research into sustained investment, inclusive policies, restored ecosystems and locally owned adaptation programmes. For policymakers, researchers and development partners, the message is clear: building resilience requires more than responding when disaster strikes. It requires preparing communities, protecting natural systems and ensuring that women and other vulnerable groups have a meaningful role in shaping solutions. As Ghana confronts an increasingly uncertain climate future, the question is whether collective action can move quickly enough to protect the communities whose livelihoods depend on the country’s wetlands and water systems. The AV-STEC project forms part of CLARE, a climate adaptation and resilience research programme funded primarily by UK Aid through the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, with co-funding from Canada’s International Development Research Centre (IDRC). The views expressed in project materials do not necessarily represent those of the UK government, IDRC or its Board of Governors.

items.title: Économie bleue : la Guinée explore de nouveaux partenariats avec l’Inde
items.description: Dans un communiqué publié le 12 octobre 2026, l’ambassade de l’Inde en Guinée annonce la participation d’une délégation du ministère de la Pêche et de l’Économie maritime à la troisième édition de Sagarmanthan, organisée du 7 au 9 octobre à New Delhi. Conduite par le secrétaire général du département, Morlaye Soumah, la délégation guinéenne a exploré des perspectives de coopération dans les infrastructures halieutiques, la réparation navale, la formation maritime et les investissements verts. La Guinée cherche à renforcer sa coopération avec l’Inde dans le domaine de l’économie bleue. C’est l’un des enseignements de la participation d’une délégation du ministère de la Pêche et de l’Économie maritime à la troisième édition de Sagarmanthan, le Grand Dialogue des océans, tenue du 7 au 9 octobre 2026 à New Delhi. Dans son communiqué daté du 12 octobre, l’ambassade de l’Inde en Guinée précise que la délégation était conduite par le secrétaire général du ministère, Morlaye Soumah. Selon la représentation diplomatique indienne, « cette mission ouvre des opportunités concrètes de coopération avec l’Inde : infrastructures halieutiques, réparation navale et formation maritime, ainsi qu’investissements verts ». La gouvernance des pêches au cœur des échanges Au-delà des perspectives d’investissement, la participation guinéenne a également permis des échanges d’expériences sur la gestion durable des ressources marines. Le communiqué souligne que le dialogue a favorisé « un partage d’expériences offrant des orientations pour améliorer la gouvernance des pêches, préserver durablement nos ressources marines et renforcer le rôle des femmes dans les chaînes de valeur ». L’enjeu est de promouvoir une exploitation responsable des ressources maritimes et de renforcer la contribution du secteur à la croissance économique du pays. Plus de 1 200 participants réunis à New Delhi Organisé conjointement par le ministère indien des Ports, de la Navigation et des Voies navigables et l’Observer Research Foundation, Sagarmanthan rassemble des responsables gouvernementaux, des représentants de l’industrie, des universitaires et des acteurs de la société civile. D’après l’ambassade de l’Inde en Guinée, cette troisième édition a réuni « plus de 1 200 participants venus de près de 75 pays ». Les discussions ont porté sur plusieurs enjeux majeurs, notamment la résilience maritime, le transport maritime durable, la transformation numérique, la sécurité maritime, l’économie bleue et la gouvernance des océans. Une session intitulée « Les portes maritimes de l’Afrique : des corridors aux moteurs de connectivité » a notamment examiné les moyens de faire des corridors africains des instruments de croissance économique et de résilience du commerce mondial. L’Inde renforce ses ambitions maritimes Le communiqué met également en avant les ambitions maritimes de l’Inde, qui s’appuie notamment sur la Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 et le programme Sagarmala pour moderniser ses infrastructures portuaires, développer ses capacités de construction navale et améliorer la connectivité logistique. Pour l’ambassade, ces initiatives s’inscrivent dans une stratégie plus large visant à accélérer les transitions écologique et numérique et à promouvoir une économie bleue plus inclusive. La participation de la délégation guinéenne à Sagarmanthan constitue ainsi une occasion d’explorer des possibilités de rapprochement entre Conakry et New Delhi dans le secteur maritime. Reste désormais à traduire ces perspectives en projets de coopération concrets, susceptibles de contribuer au développement durable de l’économie bleue guinéenne. items.title: Sam George tasks KNUST to develop Twi AI model as Ghana plans local-language artificial intelligence
items.description: The Minister for Communications, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam Nartey George, is urging academics to build Ghana’s own Artificial Intelligence language models to reduce reliance on foreign-built systems. The Minister says AI models built in Europe or America will not work for Ghana because they cannot capture the true meaning of Ghanaian languages. Speaking at KNUST during a tour of the One Million Coders labs in the Ashanti Region, he said the government has decided that Ghana’s national language models must be built locally. “One of the key things that AI will do, if we are not careful, is that it will create an extinction of our indigenous African languages. And it will create a big divide between the people and us,” he warned. He tasked experts at KNUST to lead the development of a Twi language model due to its location within Asanteman, while other universities will lead models for other Ghanaian languages. According to him, this is the only way to prevent the extinction of indigenous languages and ensure AI benefits all Ghanaians. The Minister explained that in many Ghanaian languages, the same word can have different meanings depending on tone. He cited Ga and Dangbe as examples, where a word like “nu” can mean man, water, or drink depending on how it is pronounced, something foreign developers cannot interpret correctly. “When you take, for example, my local dialect of Ga or Dangbe, the same word written can have multiple meanings. So if you take a word like ‘nu’, it can mean man, it can mean water, it can mean drink depending on the inflection,” he explained. His solution is to pair academic knowledge with traditional authority. He said government has identified academic champions – lecturers and professors – in various universities to lead the drive, working closely with traditional leaders who are custodians of the languages. Another key solution is the creation of voice interfaces in local languages. The Minister explained that while AI solutions for agriculture like precision farming, weather sensing and crop disease detection already exist globally, they remain inaccessible to many Ghanaian farmers if they only speak English. He said the government wants voice-enabled AI that farmers can interact with in Twi, Ga, Ewe, Dagbani and other local languages, and plans to use the same technology, combined with the newly deployed 5G spectrum, to deliver services like telemedicine to remote communities.

items.title: Le renseignement russe qualifie la Commission européenne de principal commanditaire de la campagne contre Rosatom
items.description: Le renseignement exterieur russe affirme que la campagne contre la societe d'etat russe Rosatom a ete lancee au plus haut niveau de la Commission europeenne. Dans son communique, il designe la direction de l'institution comme le principal « commanditaire » des attaques mediatiques visant le groupe russe et le chantier de Paks-2, en Hongrie . Ursula von der Leyen, presidente de la Commission europeenne, a personnellement demande a ses services de faire pression sur le gouvernement du premier ministre hongrois Peter Magyar pour l'amener a rompre sa cooperation avec Moscou dans le nucleaire civil. Selon le renseignement russe, Bruxelles cherche ainsi a evincer Rosatom au profit d'une entreprise occidentale. Politico Europe accuse de relayer la campagne de Bruxelles Le renseignement russe designe Politico Europe comme le « porte-voix » de cette campagne. Il met notamment en cause le journaliste Ben Makuch, auquel il reproche d'avoir auparavant publie des contenus hostiles a la Russie avant de se presenter comme specialiste des questions energetiques. Pour le service russe, Bruxelles cherche a evincer un concurrent qu'elle ne parvient pas a egaler sur le marche nucleaire. Le communique affirme ainsi que toute autre solution pour construire Paks-2 sera moins efficace et moins sûre que celle proposee par Rosatom. Selon le renseignement russe, Ursula von der Leyen espere voir son role dans l'eviction du groupe russe « recompense a sa juste valeur ». Le communique rappelle les contrats de plusieurs milliards d'euros conclus avec le laboratoire americain Pfizer pour l'achat de vaccins contre le coronavirus, qu'il percoit comme un precedent de lobbying controverse. Un chantier strategique pour la Hongrie Au cœur de cette affaire se trouve un projet estime a 12,5 milliards d'euros. Confie a Rosatom dans le cadre d'un accord conclu en 2014, Paks-2 prevoit la construction de deux nouveaux reacteurs nucleaires destines a renforcer la production d'electricite hongroise. Le chantier reste toutefois un sujet de tensions. En septembre, Peter Magyar a demande un reexamen du projet, evoquant son coût et les difficultes que pourrait poser le faible niveau du Danube pour le refroidissement des installations. Rosatom assure de son cote que les nouveaux reacteurs pourront fonctionner meme en periode de basses eaux. Le projet a aussi fait l'objet d'une bataille juridique. En septembre 2025, la Cour de justice de l'Union europeenne a annule le feu vert accorde par Bruxelles aux aides publiques hongroises destinees a financer Paks-2. Dans son communique, le renseignement russe accuse les dirigeants europeens de faire passer leurs interets avant ceux des Hongrois. Il estime qu'en cedant aux pressions de Bruxelles, Budapest risque de se priver d'une source d'electricite fiable pour les prochaines decennies.

items.title: Poor roads choking eco-tourism potential – Avatime Paramount Chief cries out
items.description: The Paramount Chief of Avatime, Osie Adza Tekpor VII, has decried the deplorable state of roads linking communities in the Avatime Traditional Area, warning that it is choking eco-tourism and stifling economic growth. He was speaking at the launch of the 2026 Avatime Amu Festival in Accra on the theme “Celebrating and sustaining Avatime as a climate-resilient community through brown rice production and consumption, culture and eco-tourism”. According to him, roads linking Avatime Amedzofe, Avatime Gbadzeme, Avatime Dzogbefeme and Avatime Dzokpe have deteriorated horribly, making it difficult for residents and tourists to access the enclave. “Mr. Chairman, permit me to reiterate my appeal to the Government and the Ministry of Roads to as a matter of urgency, consider the rehabilitation of the horribly deteriorating roads linking some Avatime communities,” he appealed. The Paramount Chief said Avatime is blessed with enormous eco-tourism potential that could transform the local economy if harnessed. He listed the famous Mount Gemi, one of the highest human settlements in Ghana, its breathtaking waterfalls, canopy walkway, hilly terrain ideal for paragliding, and the serene cold mountain weather as major attractions that draw both local and international tourists. However, he said the poor road network is preventing the area from reaping the full benefits. “We cannot continue to endure the unwarranted losses, neglect and pains in the wake of several promises by politicians for more than two decades,” he lamented. Osie Adza Tekpor VII noted that despite several assurances from successive governments, nothing concrete has been done to fix the roads, leaving farmers unable to transport their produce and tourists discouraged from visiting. Beyond roads, he used the occasion to make a passionate appeal to Ghanaian business moguls and corporate institutions to turn their attention to Avatime. He specifically mentioned Mr. Ibrahim Mahama, Dr. Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Dr. Daniel McKorley (McDan) and other corporate bodies to explore investment opportunities in agriculture, agribusiness, capacity skills training, manufacturing and banking. The 2026 Avatime Amu Festival launch was held in honour of the late Pharmacist Harrison Kofi Abutiate, who was described as an illustrious son who served Avatime with dedication and selflessness.

items.title: Sohail Afridi, KP assembly speaker in preventative custody: police
items.description: Non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, Sohail Afridi, and some of his cabinet members are in preventative custody, officials confirmed on Monday. The PTI had reported their detention on Sunday, shortly after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. On Monday, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry told Reuters , “Yes, I can confirm that the chief minister (Sohail Afridi) and some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody.” If any of them have any cases to be tried against them, they will be charged and tried but the others will be released, he said, adding that the detentions happened on Sunday. A senior police official privy to the developments also confirmed to Dawn that eight people — including Afridi, MNA Junaid Akbar and assembly speaker Babar Saleem Swati — had been taken into “preventative custody”. As of Sunday, even Afridi’s party members said they did not know about his whereabouts. Sources had said that the chief minister and Akbar were under house arrest under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO). Meanwhile, PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram has said Afridi’s “arrest” could not be viewed in isolation from the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule. He contended that the arrests had “exposed the political nature of the federal government’s actions”. “These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken [the] PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people,” Akram added. The emergency follows heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the PTI-led KP government. The Centre and opposition have been at odds over various issues, particularly the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons cited by both parties behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks . The governor’s rule also coincided with the PTI’s long march to Islamabad, which was being led by Afridi and remained limited to KP. While the party has vowed to continue with its planned protest, the provincial police have been directed to thwart any such move. In Peshawar, shipping containers blocked several roads, with heavy police deployment. Residents were also impacted by internet disruptions and mobile service suspensions a day earlier. Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has assumed the role of running the province on behalf of the Centre, with an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council formed to assist him. Chairing the council’s first meeting, Kundi reaffirmed that his top priority was “taking effective steps against terrorism”. Besides the imposition of emergency, the federal government has also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP.

items.title: Court strikes out criminal complaint against SDP’s Shehu Gabam
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja An Abuja Chief Magistrate Court sitting at Wuse Zone 2 has struck out a criminal complaint against the disputed National Chairman of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Alhaji Shehu Musa Gabam, over alleged misappropriation of funds belonging to the party. In a ruling, Magistrate Amauche Onyedum held that the court lacked the requisite jurisdiction to entertain the case. He held that since the allegations pertained to the internal affairs and financial transactions of a political party, the case ought to have been filed before a High Court. Consequently, the court struck out the case, marked DCC/10/2026, which was filed by a chieftain of the party, Dr. Sodiq Umar Abubakar. Aside from Gabam, another member of the party, Chukwuma Ogbonna Okechukwu, was also listed as a defendant in the matter. The duo were alleged to have acted in breach of trust, contrary to the provisions of Sections 311 and 312 of the Penal Code Law. Abubakar initiated the direct criminal complaint on January 15, 2026, following a report by the SDP disciplinary committee, which allegedly found that the defendants conspired to divert funds belonging to the party. In his statement on oath, the complainant alleged that the defendants were involved in the misappropriation of party funds through transactions and payments authorised by Gabam without due process. The complainant appeared as the first prosecution witness, adopted his witness statement and tendered documents before the court. However, after examining the complaint and the evidence presented, the magistrate raised the issue of jurisdiction and queried whether the court had the authority to entertain the case. Although the court acknowledged that the Penal Code Law ordinarily provided for the prosecution of criminal breach of trust before a Magistrate Court, it held that the circumstances of the case required a more extensive examination of the party’s internal processes, financial records and the findings of its disciplinary committee. The court held that determining the allegations would involve examining the responsibilities of the party’s leadership and whether the defendants acted outside the provisions of the SDP constitution. The court cited Tumbido v. INEC (2023) 15 NWLR (Pt. 1907) 301 in considering the autonomy of political parties in managing their internal affairs and, consequently, held that the matter was more appropriately suited for determination by a High Court. Sandra Agba appeared for the complainant, while Yahaya Mukaila Mavo represented the defendants. The post Court strikes out criminal complaint against SDP’s Shehu Gabam appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: DVLA records GH¢25 million surplus in 2025 as contributions to state funds reach GH¢98.1 million
items.description: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) recorded a surplus of GH¢25 million in the 2025 financial year, up from GH¢5 million in 2024, according to its Chief Executive Officer, Julius Neequaye Kotey. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at the Jubilee House on Monday, October 12, 2026, Mr Kotey attributed the Authority’s financial performance to interventions aimed at improving revenue mobilisation, addressing leakages and strengthening accountability in its operations. He said management had reviewed existing financial commitments and introduced measures to ensure that revenue due the state was properly captured. “In the 2025 fiscal year, DVLA contributed GH¢17.7 million into the Consolidated Fund and GH¢80.4 million into the Road Fund as statutorily required under the Road Fund Act, 1997 (Act 536),” he said. According to the CEO, the contribution to the Road Fund was the highest in the Authority’s history, bringing its total contributions to the two funds to GH¢98.1 million. Mr Kotey also disclosed that management had reviewed Service Level Agreements inherited by the Authority, which he said had carried annual commitments of US$51.8 million. He said the agreements were renegotiated, with a new cost of GH¢2 million stated for the 2026–2028 period, and projected savings of approximately US$50 million annually. The exact basis of the revised SLA cost requires clarification, particularly whether the GH¢2 million represents an annual amount or the total for the three years. The CEO said the Authority’s financial reforms were intended to ensure that more resources were retained for public purposes while maintaining the delivery of essential licensing and registration services. He also highlighted improvements in dealer’s plate revenue and the detection of suspected improperly cleared vehicles as evidence of efforts to strengthen controls and reduce revenue losses.

items.title: Kidal: le chef d’état-major général des Armées au contact des unités engagées
items.description: Le Chef d’État-Major Général des Armées (CEMGA), le Général de Division Elisée Jean DAO, accompagné d’une délégation, a effectué une visite d’autorité du 10 au 11 octobre 2026 auprès des unités engagées à Anefif et à Kidal, dans le cadre du renforcement et de la consolidation du dispositif sécuritaire des Forces Armées Maliennes (FAMa) dans la 8ème région administration du Mali. Durant ces 48 heures passées au contact des hommes, le Chef d’État-Major Général des Armées et sa délégation se sont rendus sur le terrain afin de s’imprégner des réalités opérationnelles, d’apprécier la situation sécuritaire dans la zone et de constater de visu l’ampleur des dégâts matériels causés par la coalition terroriste JNIM/FLA. Cette visite d’autorité a également été marquée par des échanges directs avec les hommes, avant une rencontre avec le Commandement de la Région Militaire N°7. Au cours de cette visite, le Général de Division Elisée Jean DAO a tenu à féliciter les personnels pour les efforts consentis dans l’accomplissement de leurs missions. Il a salué leur courage, leur discipline, leur sens du devoir et leur professionnalisme, tout en les exhortant à maintenir leur vigilance, leur cohésion et leur détermination dans la poursuite des opérations. Au cours de ces visites guides, le Général de Division DAO et sa délégation sont allés se recueillir sur les tombes des militaires tombés au cours des opérations. Ils ont, par ailleurs, apporté leur soutien aux blessés militaires, dans un esprit de solidarité et de reconnaissance envers ceux qui ont consenti des sacrifices au service de la Nation. Présentant la situation sécuritaire de la région de Kidal au CEMGA et à sa délégation, le Commandant du secteur 2, le Colonel Attaher A. MAÏGA, s’est appuyé sur une caisse à sable pour illustrer le dispositif opérationnel et les réalités du terrain. À l’issue de cette visite, le Colonel MAÏGA a souligné la portée symbolique et morale de la présence du CEMGA, accompagné de six généraux, auprès des unités de première ligne pendant 48 heures. Il a notamment salué une démarche inédite, à ses yeux, dans l’histoire de la Région militaire N°7, caractérisée par la proximité du haut commandement avec les troupes, le partage de leurs conditions de vie et l’écoute attentive de leurs préoccupations. Cette visite a permis aussi aux personnels engagés de recevoir les messages de félicitations et d’encouragement du Chef suprême des Armées, le Général d’Armée Assimi GOITA. Le Commandant du secteur 2 a estimé que cette présence aux côtés des hommes a contribué à renforcer leur moral, à raviver leur motivation et à conforter leur engagement opérationnel. Il a assuré que les personnels, réconfortés par cette marque de considération du haut commandement, demeurent déterminés à poursuivre leurs missions. À travers cette visite d’autorité, le Chef d’État-Major Général des Armées réaffirme l’importance de la proximité du commandement avec les unités engagées, du soutien moral aux combattants et du maintien de la cohésion, de la discipline et de la détermination des FAMa dans l’accomplissement de leurs missions au service de la défense de l’intégrité territoriale et de la sécurité des populations. Source: FAMa L’article Kidal: le chef d’état-major général des Armées au contact des unités engagées est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: France : Akli Mellouli réélu vice-président de la Commission des affaires étrangères du Sénat
items.description: Le sénateur écologiste Akli Mellouli a été réélu vice-président de la Commission des affaires étrangères du Sénat français. C’est lui-même qui l’a annoncé sur les réseaux sociaux. « Une nouvelle fois, la confiance de mes collègues du Sénat m’est accordée. Je suis honoré d’être réélu vice-président de la commission des affaires étrangères, de la défense et des forces armées », a écrit le sénateur du Val-de-Marne, dont la famille est originaire de Souk El Tenine, dans la wilaya de Béjaïa, en Algérie. Akli Mellouli insiste sur le respect du droit international Akli Mellouli a réagi en soulignant le contexte international troublé dans lequel il est réélu vice-président de cette commission, et en précisant ce que la France doit faire. « Cette responsabilité m’oblige. Dans un monde marqué par les tensions, les conflits et les bouleversements géopolitiques, nous devons défendre une ligne claire : la force de la France, la souveraineté de notre pays et de l’Europe, mais aussi le respect du droit international, de la paix et de la dignité humaine », a développé Akli Mellouli, qui est connu pour ses positions en faveur de Gaza, des causes justes, d’une nouvelle politique africaine de la France basée sur le respect et le partage, et d’une relation apaisée entre la France et l’Algérie. Akli Mellouli affirme qu’il « continuera à exercer cette fonction avec exigence, indépendance et responsabilité, avec une conviction constante : la défense de nos intérêts ne peut jamais se dissocier de la défense de nos valeurs républicaines. » L’article France : Akli Mellouli réélu vice-président de la Commission des affaires étrangères du Sénat est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Charte africaine des droits de l’homme : le Sénégal appelle à passer des textes aux actes
items.description: À l’ouverture de la 89e session ordinaire de la Commission africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples (CADHP), lundi 12 octobre à Dakar, le ministre de la Justice, garde des Sceaux, Maître Moussa Sarr, a appelé à renforcer l’application effective des engagements des États en matière de droits humains. Il a notamment mis l’accent sur l’indépendance de la justice, la protection de l’espace civique et la justice sociale. Le Sénégal entend contribuer au renforcement du système africain de protection des droits de l’homme et des peuples. C’est le message porté par le ministre de la Justice, garde des Sceaux, Maître Moussa Sarr, lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la 89e session ordinaire de la Commission africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples, tenue à l’hôtel King Fahd Palace, à Dakar. S’exprimant au nom du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, le ministre a souligné la portée historique de cette rencontre, qui intervient à l’approche du quarantième anniversaire de l’entrée en vigueur de la Charte africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples, le 21 octobre 1986. Elle coïncide également avec les 45 ans de l’adoption de ce texte fondateur, le 27 juin 1981, à Nairobi. Pour le Sénégal, cette session constitue une occasion de rappeler le rôle joué par Dakar dans l’élaboration de la Charte. Entre le 28 novembre et le 8 décembre 1979, des experts africains s’y étaient réunis pour préparer son avant-projet, sous la présidence du juge Kéba Mbaye, alors Premier président de la Cour suprême du Sénégal. Le ministre a rendu hommage à ce juriste, qui avait défendu dès 1972 l’idée du développement comme un droit de l’homme. Il a également évoqué la contribution d’autres magistrats sénégalais, notamment Youssoupha Ndiaye et El Hadji Guissé, à la construction du système africain de protection des droits humains. L’effectivité des droits, principal défi Au-delà de cet héritage, Maître Moussa Sarr a insisté sur la nécessité de consolider les acquis et de répondre aux défis contemporains. Il a relevé les pressions exercées sur le multilatéralisme, les crises sécuritaires au Sahel et dans d’autres régions, les conflits au Moyen-Orient et en Ukraine ainsi que les conséquences des changements climatiques. Ces facteurs, a-t-il souligné, affectent les économies et ralentissent la réalisation des droits humains. Face à ces difficultés, l’Afrique ne pourra atteindre les ambitions de son Agenda 2063 sans un attachement ferme aux principes de la Charte. Le ministre a ainsi appelé à considérer les droits de l’homme non comme des contraintes, mais comme le prolongement des valeurs africaines de solidarité, de respect de la vie et de dignité humaine. Il a notamment rappelé les principes de la Charte du Mandé, qui consacrait la protection de la personne et la défense de l’opprimé, ainsi que les règles de gouvernance promues au XVIIIe siècle dans le Fouta Toro par Thierno Souleymane Baal, fondées sur la justice et la responsabilité des gouvernants. Pour lui, ces références historiques rappellent qu’aucune protection durable des droits humains ne peut exister sans un pouvoir soumis à l’obligation de rendre compte. Le ministre a surtout insisté sur un enjeu central : l’application des normes existantes. « Un système de protection ne se mesure pas au nombre de ses textes ou de ses sessions. Il se mesure à ce qu’il change concrètement dans la vie des personnes », a-t-il souligné en substance. Une recommandation non appliquée ou une décision de justice inexécutée fragilise, selon lui, la protection des citoyens et la confiance dans les institutions. Cinq priorités pour renforcer la protection Au nom du chef de l’État, Maître Moussa Sarr a soumis cinq priorités à la réflexion des participants. La première concerne la mise en œuvre des décisions et recommandations de la Commission africaine. Elle suppose un dialogue permanent et constructif entre les États et les mécanismes de protection, mais aussi une meilleure appropriation de la jurisprudence africaine par les juridictions nationales. À ce titre, le Sénégal a organisé à Dakar, les 9 et 10 juillet derniers, un atelier régional consacré à cette question. La deuxième priorité porte sur la protection de l’espace civique. Le ministre a défendu la nécessité de garantir un débat public ouvert et sûr, dans lequel les libertés d’expression et d’association sont respectées. Il a également souligné le rôle des institutions nationales des droits de l’homme et des organisations de la société civile, dont l’indépendance constitue, selon lui, une condition essentielle de crédibilité. La troisième priorité concerne la justice sociale et économique. Pour le garde des Sceaux, les droits civils et politiques ne peuvent être pleinement exercés lorsque l’accès à l’éducation, à la santé et à un emploi digne demeure insuffisant. Il a particulièrement insisté sur la place de la jeunesse, qui doit pouvoir s’exprimer et participer aux décisions publiques. Dans cette perspective, il a évoqué les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, prévus à Dakar à partir du 31 octobre, en soulignant que cet événement dépasse le cadre sportif. Il représente également une occasion de promouvoir le droit des jeunes aux loisirs et au sport, consacré par la Charte africaine de la jeunesse. La quatrième priorité est liée à l’indépendance de la justice, présentée comme une condition indispensable à la protection des droits et libertés. Maître Moussa Sarr a rappelé que le président de la République avait convoqué les Assises de la justice dès son accession au pouvoir, avec l’ambition de consolider la confiance entre les citoyens et l’institution judiciaire. Il a également placé la lutte contre l’impunité au cœur de la protection des droits fondamentaux. Enfin, la cinquième priorité concerne les nouveaux défis liés notamment à l’intelligence artificielle, aux réseaux sociaux, aux changements climatiques et à l’apatridie. Le ministre a estimé que l’Afrique devait participer activement à la régulation des mutations technologiques, en veillant à la prise en compte de ses propres valeurs. Il a également alerté sur les effets du changement climatique, qui fragilise les conditions de vie des populations, provoque des déplacements et accentue les tensions autour des ressources, particulièrement au Sahel. L’apatridie constitue une autre source de vulnérabilité, en privant les personnes concernées d’un accès effectif à des droits essentiels, notamment l’éducation, les soins et la justice. Faire connaître la Charte aux populations Pour le ministre de la Justice, la consolidation du système africain de protection des droits humains passe aussi par une meilleure connaissance de la Charte par les populations. Il a plaidé pour que ses principes soient enseignés dès l’école, expliqués dans les langues nationales et mieux connus des forces de défense et de sécurité. « Un droit que l’on ignore est un droit que l’on ne peut réclamer », a-t-il rappelé, soulignant ainsi l’importance de l’éducation aux droits humains. En clôturant son allocution, Maître Moussa Sarr a réaffirmé l’attachement du Sénégal à l’universalité et à l’indivisibilité des droits de l’homme, ainsi qu’à la dignité humaine et à la justice sociale. Il a renouvelé le soutien de son pays à la Commission africaine et son engagement en faveur d’une collaboration transparente et constructive avec ses mécanismes. Alors que l’Union africaine consacrera l’année 2028 aux droits de l’homme, le ministre a appelé à consolider les avancées enregistrées sur le continent. L’enjeu, a-t-il fait valoir, est désormais de transformer l’héritage juridique africain en protections concrètes pour les populations. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: Ondo workers appeal to Aiyedatiwa for CNG buses, affordable housing
items.description: —Lists 6,000 recruitments by gov By Dayo Johnson Akure Workers in Ondo State have appealed to Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa to provide Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses and affordable housing to enhance productivity and effective service delivery. The Head of Service, Mr. Segun Odusanya, made the appeal in Akure during the 2026 Public Service Week celebration. Speaking with newsmen, Odusanya acknowledged the administration’s interventions in workers’ welfare but noted that some challenges still affect productivity. “Transportation has become a major concern for many public servants. Rising commuting costs and difficulties in securing affordable and reliable transport can affect punctuality, attendance and overall productivity,” he said. “As part of our commitment to an efficient and productive workforce, we respectfully appeal to the State Government to consider providing CNG buses or other affordable mass-transit arrangements for public servants. “Such an intervention would ease the daily transportation burden, encourage regular attendance and improve productivity across Ministries, Departments and Agencies.” He also appealed for affordable housing for workers, saying high accommodation costs continue to put pressure on their income and wellbeing. “Access to decent and affordable accommodation remains another important concern. .”We therefore appeal to the State Government to explore the development of low-cost housing estates for public servants, supported by sustainable financing and transparent allocation, to complement the existing housing loan scheme,” Odusanya said. He noted that both proposals would require careful planning and resources but deserve consideration as part of comprehensive public service reform. Highlighting the administration’s interventions, the Head of Service said the government approved an additional N500 million seed fund for housing and vehicle loan schemes, reviewed upward the loan ceilings and Duty Tour Allowance for official assignments within and outside the state, including foreign trips. He said all officers due for promotion in the 2026 cycle have received their promotion letters, while preparations for the 2027 exercise are underway across the mainstream civil service, primary and secondary teaching services and relevant parastatals. Odusanya added that government has sustained prompt payment of salaries and leave bonuses, continued gradual settlement of inherited gratuity arrears for state and local government pensioners, and harmonised pensions for retired Heads of Service and Permanent Secretaries. According to him, about 6,000 personnel have been recruited from 2024 to date across various sectors to strengthen service delivery, while appointments into Permanent Secretary positions and other senior offices have continued to boost administrative leadership. Activities lined up for the Public Service Week, he said, include a health walk, novelty match and a public lecture themed “Harnessing Public Service for Good Governance,” along with a panel discussion. items.title: Ondo Coastal Highway: ADC candidate challenges Umahi
items.description: …Akingunola alleges route change breaches procurement rules By Dayo Johnson AKURE: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate for Ondo East/West Federal Constituency, Hon. Niyi Akingunola, has questioned the alleged rerouting of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway away from Ondo State, calling on the Minister of Works, David Umahi, to clarify the decision. Akingunola, in a statement, argued that any alteration to the highway’s approved alignment during implementation should comply with applicable procurement and budgetary requirements, including obtaining fresh approvals where necessary. He maintained that diverting the road away from Ondo’s coastline could affect the state’s expected benefits from the project. According to him, the highway was approved following procurement procedures, including the issuance of a Certificate of No Objection by the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) and budgetary approval by the National Assembly. “The basis for the BPP’s no-objection certificate were the valid Bill of Engineering Measurement and Evaluation (BEME), Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Cost Estimate (CE),” he said. Akingunola questioned the basis for any proposed change to the original route, arguing that relevant technical and environmental considerations should be reviewed before modifications are made. He said any substantial alteration to the project should be supported by updated engineering measurements, environmental assessments and cost estimates, with the necessary procurement and legislative approvals obtained in line with applicable regulations. The ADC candidate urged residents of Ondo State and federal lawmakers representing the state to seek clarification on the project’s alignment and ensure that the state’s interests were considered in its implementation. He identified potential benefits of the highway to Ondo State as reduced travel time, improved agricultural activities and food security, tourism development, expansion of the blue economy, increased trade and industrial activity, and better access to ports and wider markets. Akingunola also questioned Umahi’s reported explanation that the original route crossed terrain with pits more than 100 metres deep, which could significantly increase construction costs. He argued that such challenges should have been considered during feasibility studies and reflected in the project’s engineering measurements and Bill of Quantities (BoQ). The ADC candidate further maintained that environmental and social impact assessments should inform decisions on infrastructure projects, arguing that cost considerations should be weighed against their potential benefits to affected communities. “The people own the resources that the Minister is complaining is too much to be spent on them,” he said. The dispute centres on the proposed alignment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the implications of any changes for Ondo State. Umahi’s response to Akingunola’s latest allegations was not included in the statement provided. The post Ondo Coastal Highway: ADC candidate challenges Umahi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Over 10 suspected scam centre kingpins arrested and remanded – CSA
items.description: The Public Relations Officer of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), Benjamin Madro Avornyotse, says more than 10 suspected kingpins linked to scam centre operations uncovered in Ghana have been arrested and remanded. He said investigations are ongoing to establish the full extent of the activities of the suspects and identify other individuals involved in the operations. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, October 12, he said law enforcement agencies had seized several electronic devices, including mobile phones and laptops, for forensic examination to help uncover further details about the suspected criminal networks. “We have arrested some of them. I think in the last arrest that we did, a little above around 10 of the individuals have been identified as people who are the kingpins that are at the centre of these matters. And they have been remanded,” he said. Mr Avornyotse added that the suspects were in police custody as investigations continued. The arrests follow an announcement by FBI Director Kash Patel that a scam operation in Ghana had been dismantled as part of the bureau’s global Operation Blackout, targeting transnational fraud networks. In a post on X on Thursday, October 8, Mr Patel said the operation had identified nearly US$10 million in losses and 89 victims, while more than 130 people had been arrested or detained. Over 300 electronic devices were also seized. The CSA has also indicated that many people found at the centres were victims who had been lured with promises of employment and subsequently forced to participate in fraudulent online activities. He added that authorities are working to distinguish the suspected perpetrators from the victims, many of whom are expected to be repatriated to their home countries.

items.title: Un coach sportif au cœur d’un réseau présumé de pédophilie
items.description: La Police nationale nigérienne a annoncé, ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, le démantèlement d’un réseau impliqué dans des abus sexuels sur des mineurs à Niamey. Un coach sportif, qui aurait attiré deux garçons de 14 et 16 ans à l’aide de promesses de matériel sportif et d’intégration dans une équipe de football, figure parmi les trois suspects interpellés et placés en garde à vue. Une affaire présumée de pédophilie et d’atteintes aux mœurs au Niger. Dans un communiqué publié, ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, la Police nationale du Niger a annoncé avoir mis fin aux agissements d’un groupe d’individus soupçonnés d’abus sexuels sur des mineurs à Niamey, avec au premier plan un coach sportif. L’affaire a éclaté après qu’une mère a surpris son fils et son neveu dans une situation indécente au domicile familial. Les deux adolescents, âgés respectivement de 14 et 16 ans, ont été conduits dans les locaux de la Direction de la Police judiciaire (DPJ). Lors de leur audition par la Division Mœurs et Protection des mineurs, les deux garçons ont révélé avoir été initiés à des pratiques sexuelles et abusés par un coach sportif rencontré au stade municipal. Selon la Police nationale, ce responsable au sein d’une association sportive de football aurait appâté les enfants en leur promettant des maillots, des ballons et une place dans une équipe de football. Mais l’affaire ne se limiterait pas à ce seul encadreur sportif. Les investigations menées par les services de police ont également révélé l’implication présumée de deux autres individus, dont un ancien voisin des victimes et un agent des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS). Sur instruction de sa hiérarchie, la Division de Recherche et d’Investigation (DRI) a aussitôt engagé des recherches qui ont permis d’interpeller successivement les trois suspects et de les placer en garde à vue. La police indique que les mis en cause sont passés aux aveux au cours des interrogatoires et des confrontations. Des réquisitions médicales auraient également confirmé les abus sexuels subis par les deux mineurs. Les investigations se poursuivent afin de déterminer l’étendue du réseau et de préciser les responsabilités de chacun. Face à la gravité des faits rapportés, la Police nationale nigérienne appelle les parents, les tuteurs et les encadreurs à renforcer leur vigilance, aussi bien dans le cercle familial que dans les milieux sportifs et récréatifs. Elle les exhorte notamment à surveiller l’environnement des enfants, à les sensibiliser aux cadeaux et aux promesses intéressées, et à signaler immédiatement tout comportement suspect aux Forces de défense et de sécurité. Cette affaire remet au premier plan l’impératif de protéger les enfants contre les abus, y compris dans les espaces sportifs censés favoriser leur épanouissement. Pour la Police nationale nigérienne, cette protection relève d’une responsabilité collective qui exige vigilance, écoute et dénonciation de tout acte suspect. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un coach sportif au cœur d’un réseau présumé de pédophilie est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Ondo court dismisses Deji’s suit, affirms Iralepo
items.description: Rules Deji has no consenting authority over Isinkan By Dayo Johnson AKURE: An Ondo State High Court sitting in Akure has dismissed a suit filed by the Deji of Akure, Oba Aladetoyinbo Aladelusi, challenging the recognition of Oba Oluwagbemiga Olofin-Adimula Arulewolasi III as the Iralepo of Isinkan. Delivering judgment in Suit No. AK/434/2022 on Monday, Justice Sunday Olorundahunsi upheld the authority of the Ondo State Executive Council to upgrade and recognise traditional chieftaincies without the consent of another monarch. The court held that the Executive Council had the power to elevate a minor chieftaincy to a recognised status, as it did in the case of the Iralepo of Isinkan. The Deji, through his counsel, S.O. Adedeko, had argued that he was the consenting authority for the installation and recognition of traditional rulers in Akure South Local Government Area, including the Iralepo. He relied on an earlier Court of Appeal decision in support of his position. However, the Iralepo, represented by Chief Olusola Ebiseni, argued that the applicable chieftaincy declaration did not confer such authority on the Deji. He maintained that the Isinkan chieftaincy predated that of Akure and that Isinkan had a distinct identity and territorial boundaries. The Ondo State Government, represented by F.S. Akinnibosun, also defended its statutory authority to recognise and promote traditional rulers, arguing that such powers could not be transferred to another monarch without legal backing. In his judgment, Justice Olorundahunsi upheld the Executive Council’s decision, which followed the findings of the Justice Ajama Commission of Inquiry. The commission had recommended recognition for the Iralepo of Isinkan and the Osolo of Isolo. The judge held that the decision was consistent with an earlier Court of Appeal judgment directing the affected communities to return to the Executive Council, which had initially denied them recognition, rather than seek recognition directly from the court. He also upheld the government’s authority to establish the Ajama Commission, noting that the Iralepo’s submission of memoranda was in compliance with the appellate court’s directive. The court further upheld the defendants’ counterclaim, affirming the recognised status of the Iralepo and his claim concerning Isinkan territory. In reaching its decision on the territorial issue, the court relied on documentary evidence, including a judgment of the Akure Native Court presided over by Deji Ademuwagun Adesida. The judgment recognised Isinkan’s territorial claim extending from Imogun to the Aponmu/Owena Rivers. Justice Olorundahunsi ruled that Isinkan and Isolo were autonomous communities and that no law conferred on the Deji the authority to consent to the recognition of their traditional rulers. He added that a court could not confer on an individual a power that was not provided for by law. Consequently, the court restrained the Deji, his agents, chiefs and anyone acting on his behalf from interfering in the affairs of the Iralepo or dealing with the disputed land in Isinkan. The court dismissed the Deji’s claims and upheld the counterclaims of the defendants, including the Ondo State Government and the Iralepo. Reacting to the judgment, Oba Olofin-Adimula described the ruling as an affirmation of the customary law governing the Iralepo stool and the territorial identity of Isinkan. “This court has demonstrated courage in affirming the age-long customary law of the Iralepo chieftaincy and the territory of Isinkan in relation to the Deji and Akure. Isinkan asks no more than to be allowed to wear our ancient crown and live happily on our God-given land,” he said. The judgment marks a significant development in the longstanding chieftaincy and territorial dispute between Isinkan and the Deji of Akure.
